title: How to Repair a Leaking Toilet: Wax Rings, Flange Height, and Spacers

locations.name: New York (caller location)
locations.basis: Transcript indicates caller is Megan in New York; filming location not specified.

summary: This Old House's Ask This Old House episode guides diagnosing a leaking toilet by examining common leak sources (water-supply connections, tank-to-bowl gasket, and flange seals), explains the wax ring’s role and how floor instability can deform it, and presents modern height-adjustment options (foam gaskets and flange spacers) to restore a proper seal. The host emphasizes securing the flange to structural supports, accurately restoring flange height to finish-floor level, and finally returning to a conventional wax seal once the height is correct, to achieve a durable, non-rocking installation.

sections.title: Initial leak diagnosis: water supply and tank-to-bowl considerations
sections.description: Introduces the leak scenario and outlines first checks: inspect the water-supply nut for visual leaks, tighten if needed; inspect the gasket between the tank and bowl and discuss leaks that show on the floor or through the ceiling.

sections.title: Closet flange basics: bolts, wax ring, and toilet-to-flange seal
sections.description: Explains how the closet flange is secured to the floor with bolts and how the wax ring forms the seal between the toilet and the flange; stresses that a level floor and proper bolt engagement are essential for a solid seal.

sections.title: Flange height, seal deformation, and wax-seal alternatives
concepts: flange height relative to finished floor
sections.description: Addresses how a rocking floor can deform wax, leading to leaks; discusses height issues caused by tile work and the need to raise the flange to original height using spacers and alternative seals like foam gaskets to maintain a proper seal before returning to conventional wax.

sections.title: Final steps: securing, restoring height, and re-installing wax seal
sections.description: Summarizes the final sequence: secure the flange to a solid substrate, use height-restoring methods (spacers or related hardware) to reach the correct height, then revert to the standard wax seal and ensure the assembly is level and non-rocking for a durable seal.

featured_techniques.technique: Identify leak sources by inspecting water-supply nut and tank-to-bowl gasket; tighten as needed
Inspect and tighten closet bolts and the gasket at the tank-to-bowl interface to seal
Wax ring function and deformation due to floor rocking; proper connection seals against sewer gas and water
Address flange height issues caused by tile work; raise flange using spacers to original height
Use foam gasket and other height-adjusting products as alternatives to wax
Return to conventional wax seal after achieving correct height and level
Ensure level floor and prevent rocking before final sealing
